haiku-low.q1: A message arriving on the domain-events topic starts work. The core app's outbox relay publishes every business event there.
haiku-low.q2: The Dispatcher inserts one pending delivery per matching active subscription. A unique key on (event_id, subscription_id) makes a redelivered duplicate insert nothing.
haiku-low.q3: HMAC-SHA256 over '<t>.<raw body>' using the subscription secret. It is computed fresh on every attempt, with the current Unix time t.
haiku-low.q4: 2xx: delivered. 408, 429, 5xx, timeout, connection error: retried until 8 attempts, then dead. 410: dead, subscription disabled. Other 4xx or 3xx: dead, no retry.
haiku-low.q5: At most 8 attempts. The third attempt is made 2 minutes after the second attempt fails.
haiku-low.q6: In the deliveries table in the service's own Postgres database. Each row holds status, attempts, next_attempt_at and last result.
haiku-low.q7: It waits as pending with next_attempt_at set in the deliveries table. Workers poll about once per second and claim rows whose time has passed.
haiku-low.q8: Its lease expires after 60 seconds and another worker claims the row and POSTs again with the same X-Webhook-Id, so the receiver may get the event twice.
haiku-low.q9: Dead deliveries stay in the deliveries table with dead_at set. Replay sets status pending, attempts 0 and next_attempt_at now, keeping the same id.
haiku-low.q10: The X-Webhook-Id header holds the delivery id. It stays the same on every attempt and every replay, so receivers can dedupe on it.
haiku-low.q11: Each pending delivery becomes cancelled when a worker next claims it, with no POST sent. A send already in flight finishes.
haiku-low.q12: Yes. The document states there is no ordering between events.

sonnet.q1: A message arriving on the `domain-events` topic starts the work; the core app's outbox relay produces it (it publishes every business event there). The Dispatcher receives it.
sonnet.q2: The Dispatcher finds active subscriptions matching the event's account_id and event type (or '*') and inserts one pending `deliveries` row per match. A unique key on (event_id, subscription_id) means a redelivered message inserts nothing new.
sonnet.q3: HMAC-SHA256 over `<t>.<raw body>` (t = current Unix time in seconds) using the subscription's secret, sent as X-Webhook-Signature `t=<t>,v1=<hex>`. It is produced again on every attempt, since receivers reject a t older than 5 minutes.
sonnet.q4: 2xx: delivered. 410: dead letter now, and the subscription is set to disabled with disabled_reason='gone'. Other 4xx or 3xx: dead now, no retry (redirects not followed). Transient (408, 429, 5xx, timeout, connection error): retried on the schedule; dead after 8 attempts.
sonnet.q5: At most 8 attempts per cycle (a replay starts a fresh cycle of 8). After attempt 2 fails, the wait is 2 minutes before attempt 3.
sonnet.q6: In the `deliveries` table in the service's own Postgres: state, `attempts`, `next_attempt_at`, `last_status_code` / `last_error` (plus lease_until, dead_at).
sonnet.q7: It waits as a `pending` row in the Postgres `deliveries` table with next_attempt_at set. Workers poll about once per second for pending rows whose next_attempt_at has passed and claim them, so the queue's 15-minute delay limit is not involved.
sonnet.q8: The 60 s lease expires and another worker claims the row and POSTs again with the same X-Webhook-Id, so the receiver may get the event twice. The attempt was already counted, so it still stops at 8.
sonnet.q9: They are held in the same `deliveries` table with state `dead` and dead_at set, kept 14 days. Replay sets state to pending, attempts = 0 and next_attempt_at = now (same delivery id), starting a fresh 8-attempt cycle. Replay is refused if the subscription is disabled.
sonnet.q10: The `X-Webhook-Id` header, which is the delivery id. It does not change between attempts or after a replay.
sonnet.q11: They are not sent. Each becomes `cancelled` when a worker next claims it, with no POST. A send already in flight finishes.
sonnet.q12: Yes. The design guarantees no ordering between events.
